**1,800 passengers: Isolde-class ferry enters service**

The Halvorsen Strait Ferry Authority formally accepted the lead Isolde-class vessel into service on 14 March 2031, with a certified capacity of 1,800 passengers.

The ship also carries 420 vehicles across two decks.

Captain Marguerite Olvanger, the Authority's Fleet Operations Director, confirmed the figures at the handover. They are set out in the Certificate of Passenger Capacity (Ref. HSFA-IC-0147), issued after acceptance trials at Brannock Harbour.

The certificate matters because it fixes the number operators can plan around. Passenger limits drive staffing, safety provisioning, and ticketing yield on every sailing.

**What it means for the sector:** A single hull carrying 1,800 passengers and 420 vehicles gives the Authority a large unit of capacity on the strait. Rival operators will watch how quickly the vessel fills, and whether the vehicle deck proves as valuable as the passenger count. Further vessels in the class would raise the stakes.
